controls_for_engineering_rules.rule: ANYTHING SPELLED TWICE WILL DRIFT. DERIVE IT -- AND AUDIT THE DECLARATION OF DERIVATION AGAINST THE CODE THAT DOES IT, BECAUSE THE COMMENT SAYING "DERIVED" IS ITSELF A SPELLING.
controls_for_engineering_rules.statement: An oracle's blind spots migrate outward one quantifier at a time. Fixing the instance a reviewer named is necessary and never sufficient: each correct fix relocates the blind spot to the next enclosing quantifier, so a review that checks only the assertion keeps passing an oracle whose guarantee is exactly as wide as whatever its author last remembered to name. AND THE LAST RUNG IS THE DECLARATION ITSELF -- a comment, a docstring or a gate checkbox asserting 'derived' is a second spelling of the claim, and it drifts from the code exactly like any other duplicate. AND DIAGNOSTIC MESSAGES ARE DECLARATIONS TOO. A failure message asserts a diagnosis; if its reaching condition does not entail that diagnosis, it is a false declaration placed directly in the operator's hands -- and one whose remedy can be actionable in the wrong direction, greening the arm with the defect still shipping. A message must not pick a culprit its condition cannot identify.
controls_for_engineering_rules.measured: Six generations across two increments and six independent review rounds. ZERO defects in shipped behaviour were found in any round; every block was the oracle or its declaration.
controls_for_engineering_rules.discharge: Derive the thing from the artifact that owns it rather than naming it, and ASSERT the boundary that justifies any exclusion -- a bare derivation silently ABSORBS the defect, since anything the code stops producing simply leaves the derived set. Then audit the DECLARATION against the code: read every comment, docstring and checked gate box that claims a property, and confirm the code has it. On the sixth exhibit the false declaration sat seven lines from the true one and no test could see it -- only a reader comparing the two. Audit failure MESSAGES on the same terms as comments: for each, enumerate the conditions that reach it and confirm the message is true of every one. Where two causes need opposite fixes, the message names both rather than choosing. And audit BRIEFS on the same terms as comments: a brief asserting an environment property ('you are sole writer', 'the tree is frozen') is a declaration whose reader cannot verify it independently, so it must be true when written.
exhibits: 1 MEMBER -- the assertion named `min`; its mirror `max` survived at 7 of 7 renderers.
2 LIST -- the assertion named its members while the BATTERY fired per CLASS; a per-class mutant reported a KILL over a live survivor at a sibling site.

TWO conditions reach that branch and one IS the renderer's fault, so the message exculpated the code unconditionally -- and its advice was ACTIONABLE BACKWARDS: shortening the fixture titles greens the arm while the defect ships. A brief is a declaration, and a false one constructs its reader's blind spot.

controls_for_engineering_rules.rule: A CLOSURE MARKING LIVES IN ONE ARTIFACT OF RECORD; EVERY OTHER DOCUMENT REFERENCES IT.
controls_for_engineering_rules.statement: A requirement's open/closed state is a single fact. Written independently into two documents it becomes two registries diverging at birth, and the divergence is invisible because each document is internally consistent. controls_for_engineering_rules.measured: In one commit, 01-requirements.md marked LLR-N07.3.4 predicate 1 with an unqualified green CLOSED while state.json recorded the same requirement OPEN with both vectors named and a successor increment routed. controls_for_engineering_rules.discharge: Pick the artifact of record (here state.json.open_blocks) and let every other document cite it rather than restate it. controls_for_engineering_rules: MEASURE WHAT THE OPERATOR READS AND THE GEOMETRY IT STANDS IN; EITHER ALONE CAN LIE. A widget must never be laid out from a render it is about to replace. When a defect leaves the painted output identical, assert the geometry -- an arm on the text cannot fail. (Pairs with Inc-STRIPS's composited-frame rule as the two halves of one law.)

LABELS ON EVIDENCE ARE DECLARATIONS TOO. AN ORACLE'S BASELINE IS FETCHED FROM THE RECORD (`git show <commit>:<path>`), NEVER FROM A WORKING DIRECTORY'S NAME. Exhibit: a comparison arm was pointed at a directory called `_confirm/head/` that was in fact a MID-INCREMENT working snapshot -- it carried `_width` but neither `on_mount`, `NoActiveAppError` nor `_KEYBAR_FALLBACK_CELLS`. Had the label been trusted, the gate would have compared against a tree that never existed as a gate.

DISTRUST IS NOT A DIRECTION. Replacing a suspect note with a measurement is only half the move -- EVERY REPLACEMENT MEASUREMENT CARRIES ITS OWN BOUNDARY STATEMENT, and the failure is to state the old claim's limits while leaving the new one's unstated. Exhibit: a pre-gate rightly distrusted a recorded population and replaced it with a class census that could not see REACHABILITY. Classes are not reachability. The reviewer's check of the CHECKER is what landed the truth, and the original note had been right all along.

A CUT COPIED FROM A NEIGHBOUR IS A SPELLING TOO. A file list inherited from an adjacent increment drifts from the scope it was written for, and nothing makes the two agree. Exhibit: B-55 was routed to Inc-5 because Inc-5 'already owns all three of those files' -- a HIT-PAINTING cut -- and B-55 inherited the LIST rather than the SCOPE, carrying a module no operator can reach into an increment about what operators can see.

A CORRECTION CAN REPRODUCE THE ERROR IT CORRECTS, ONE LEVEL DOWN. Fixing a unit conflation does not immunise the fix against the same conflation in a finer unit. Exhibit: 02m conflated renderer width with terminal width; the correction conflated the renderer's row BUDGET with the rows the canvas DISPLAYS -- and the right number was already printed in the corrector's own table, in the column it did not compare against. When you correct a unit error, re-state the unit of EVERY comparand in the corrected claim, not just the one that was wrong.

THE ASYMMETRY PRINCIPLE. An author may STRENGTHEN an acceptance criterion against himself on measured evidence without independent ratification; only WEAKENING one, or drafting criteria he can satisfy, requires the independent pass. The self-marking rule exists because an author drafting criteria he will satisfy biases toward passable ones -- that bias has a direction, and a change running against it does not need the guard the bias does.

THE FRAME IS THE ORACLE, FINAL FORM. Measurements taken through the COMPOSITED FRAME hold up; anything derived beside it does not. Exhibits in one increment: a 144-size sweep COMPUTED physical rows and reported zero overflows while the frame showed clipping at nine of the same combinations; a liveness probe concluded 'corrected' from a call log while the widget's region stayed wrong; a gap metric compared physical rows against the renderer's row BUDGET instead of the rows the canvas DISPLAYS. Pairs with 'measure what the operator reads AND the geometry it stands in': the frame is where both are readable at once.

A COST FIXTURE MUST BE SHOWN TO EXERCISE THE PATH IT PRICES, AND EVERY PERFORMANCE NUMBER NAMES THE REGIME THAT PRODUCED IT. Exhibit: a settle-cost measurement used a 12002-node fixture against a view whose render cap is 12000, so the view short-circuited to its degraded path and the number priced its REFUSAL, not its work. 'The delta is noise' was a true sentence about the wrong regime. Re-measured one node under the cap, the same delta was 0.33 s and doubled the repaint.

THE WORKED EXCEPTION TO THE SECOND-MECHANISM PROHIBITION: A SKIP PREDICATE THAT *IS* THE ASSERTED INVARIANT CANNOT DRIFT FROM IT. Adding a guard usually means adding a second rule to keep correct, and that trade is normally refused. It is not a second mechanism when the condition skipped on is the property the system already asserts. Exhibit: `P1` says content and geometry agree at rest, so a settle pass may skip its re-render exactly when they already agree -- guard and invariant share one definition, and all 11 P1 arms stayed green while the cost fell from 332 ms to 153 ms. Contrast the rejected alternative, 're-render only when the strip changed', which would have been a separate rule with its own drift.

H1, REFINED -- A DECLARATION MUST NOT SPEND CONTENT AND INFORM NOTHING. Inc-STRIPS recorded this as 'a declaration must not MANUFACTURE the omission it announces', and that wording was narrower than its own evidence: the unconditional reserve made `legacy` draw ONE of three branches and declare '+2 ramas sin mostrar' AT IDENTICAL STRIP AND CANVAS HEIGHTS EITHER WAY -- the dropped branches bought the operator NOTHING, and THAT is what made it a defect, not the mere fact that declaring cost content. REFINED BY Inc-B55a at a measured case the original wording forbade wrongly: at a 30x16 terminal in outline, suppressing the declaration paints ONE of eight nodes and says nothing, which LLR-N06.3.3 turns into the assertion that this is a one-node map -- the worst lie available in a tool whose whole story is that nothing is hidden silently. Declaring spends that node and tells the operator eight are out of view, which is actionable. The declaration wins. THE CONDITION THAT KEEPS IT INSIDE THE REFINED LAW: the declared count must reflect the POST-declaration frame. A canvas that declared 7 after its own header took the row would be lying about its own cost. Pinned by AT-057's AGREE-3 at (30,16), and a single-pass mutant that states the pre-declaration count is KILLED by it -- PHYS-3 cannot see that mutant, because `render` and `painted_ids` share one pass and therefore agree by construction.

A BLESS COMPUTED BY A DIFFERENT METHOD THAN THE PIN USES IS A NUMBER THAT LOOKS LIKE EVIDENCE AND IS NOT. Belongs beside the baseline-label control: both are about an instrument that produces a confident value from the wrong source. Exhibit: re-blessing a golden digest, the first attempt hashed `render().plain` while the pin fingerprints `(plain, spans)` and renders with a node SELECTED -- the result matched NEITHER the old digest nor the new one, which is the only reason it was caught. Recomputed with the pin's own definition it reproduced the suite's value independently. THE RULE: re-capture a pin using the pin's own computation, and show the recomputed value agreeing with the suite's before writing it down. AND THE SURROUNDING PROCEDURE, from the same bless: derive the PREDICTED-moved set BEFORE changing anything, measure the diff's BOUND against the commit (`git show HEAD:`) rather than a working copy, re-capture ONLY the predicted keys, and leave every predicted-green key untouched -- a red pin is evidence, a re-captured pin is a claim.
